concerns.text: The mixed‑effects specification includes a random intercept for RunnerID only. Game-level heterogeneity (e.g., unobserved game characteristics beyond the external difficulty label) is not modeled as a random effect, risking omitted‑variable bias when estimating the effect of GameDifficulty.

The model does not include the run category (e.g., any% vs 100%) as a covariate, although category can substantially affect run times and may confound the relationship between difficulty/pressure and performance.

Competitive pressure is proxied by the count of active runners in the prior 30 days, but no justification or validation of this proxy is provided. Without evidence that this metric captures the intended construct, construct validity of the pressure variable is questionable.

FR‑009 (power statement) is marked `[deferred]`. Given the modest number of games (10–15) and the intention to detect game‑level difficulty effects, a concrete power analysis (or at least a minimum detectable effect size) is required to ensure the study is adequately powered; deferring this undermines the claim that the analysis will be statistically informative.

Potential time‑trend confounds (e.g., overall improvement in community skill over calendar time) are not addressed. Lagged competitive pressure mitigates endogeneity but does not control for secular trends that could bias the estimated learning‑curve parameters.
